sql_schemas: table leave_requests | fields: id, employee_id, leave_type, start_date, end_date, status, reason, manager_id, rejection_reason, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employees.id; manager_id -> employees.id | indexes: employee_id: frequent lookups of all leave requests for a given employee; status: filtering by pending/approved/rejected status for manager dashboards; leave_type: filtering by leave type for balance calculations and reporting; start_date, end_date: date-range queries for overlapping leave detection and calendar views; manager_id: manager dashboard queries listing requests needing their approval

table leave_balances | fields: id, employee_id, leave_type, year, total_allocated, used_days, pending_days, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employees.id | indexes: employee_id, leave_type, year: unique composite lookup for balance queries per employee per leave type per year; employee_id: all balance queries for a given employee

table leave_policies | fields: id, leave_type, days_per_year, max_consecutive_days, requires_attachment, allow_negative_balance, accrual_enabled, accrual_rate_per_month, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | indexes: leave_type: unique lookup of policy rules by leave type

table employees | fields: id, email, full_name, role, manager_id, department, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: manager_id -> employees.id | indexes: email: unique login lookup; role: RBAC enforcement queries; manager_id: direct-reports queries for manager dashboards; department: departmental leave reports

table audit_logs | fields: id, entity_type, entity_id, action, actor_id, changes, timestamp | pk: id | fks: actor_id -> employees.id | indexes: entity_type, entity_id: audit trail lookups for a specific record; actor_id: audit queries by user; timestamp: time-range audit queries; action: filtering audit logs by action type (create, update, delete)

data_notes: Persistence slice designed with 5 conceptual tables: leave_requests, leave_balances, leave_policies, employees, and audit_logs. Three repository interfaces defined: ILeaveRequestRepository (PgLeaveRequestRepository), ILeaveBalanceRepository (PgLeaveBalanceRepository), ILeavePolicyRepository (PgLeavePolicyRepository) — all backed by PostgreSQL via the existing pg Pool at src/shared/db/connection.ts. Two open questions recorded: fractional-day handling and leave-year boundary definition.

open_questions.question: How are partial-day leave durations counted and rounded in balance calculations (e.g., half-day leave = 0.5 days)?
open_questions.impact: Affects the data type used for used_days/pending_days in leave_balances and the increment/decrement repository methods. If fractional days are allowed, all balance arithmetic must use decimal semantics; if only whole days, rounding rules (floor/ceil/nearest) must be specified.
candidate_options: Whole days only — reject fractional-day requests
Fractional days allowed — store as decimal with 0.5 granularity
Fractional days allowed — store as decimal with any precision

open_questions.question: What defines the leave year boundary for balance allocation and reset?
open_questions.impact: Determines how the `year` field in leave_balances is computed and when balances reset. Affects the `findByEmployeeAndTypeAndYear` lookup logic and the accrual schedule.
candidate_options: Rolling 12-month window from employee start date
